speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned you have persistent vomiting and chest pain; let's start by asking: have you experienced any shortness of breath, sweating, or radiation of pain to your jaw or arm?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome (Esophageal Rupture)

The history of forceful vomiting followed by coughing and chest pain is classic for an esophageal tear. Given the severity of your symptoms and inability to communicate, I am requesting immediate imaging to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_Xray and Chest_CTA.
